question: Can money saved for a cancelled Hajj be used for other expenses during financial hardship?
asked: She was planning to go for Hajj, but now the government has announced that the Hajj has been cancelled. She had saved up some money. Is she sinful in taking that money and using it for her other expenses, given that their situation is not as financially strong as it was because of the COVID crisis?
answer:
Now, the question that our sister had was that she had set aside some money, and now most travel agents are able to return it partially or fully. And again, this is up to you and the travel agent. If they're not able to return it fully, then again, that is their prerogative in business, and you need to go to them and find out what can or cannot be done. That's not a shar'i issue; it's a logistical issue.

But the question now comes: our sister is saying that she had this money saved up for Hajj. She had intended to spend it for Hajj. Now the money is there, whether it was refunded or whether she didn't give the full amount; now she has that money. But she needs that money because the COVID crisis has affected her or her husband's, or whatever, financial situation. And now she's wondering, is it permissible to utilize that money for her daily expenses?

And the response is, **there is absolutely no sin on you to utilize this money, because circumstances have changed.** The money does not become earmarked and demarcated such that you no longer have access to it. Rather, the circumstances changed, and so the status of the money changes as well.

Now, obviously, if you have saved up for this Hajj and you are able to keep this amount for next year's Hajj, then you should do that, because Hajj is obligatory as soon as one is able to go. This is the stronger position. There are two positions in Islamic fiqh: can you delay Hajj for no reason, or should you do Hajj as soon as you're financially capable?

There's a hadith in ad-Daraqutni, slightly weak, that somebody asked the Prophet ﷺ when basically you're supposed to go for Hajj, and he said, "Az-zad wa ar-rahilah." Now, the hadith is weak, but some say the concept is from the Sahabah, and it is something that makes sense. Az-zad wa ar-rahilah means that you need to have enough money to take care of you on the way and on the way back, and you need to have an animal or transportation to take you there as well.

So what has happened now is that you had the money, the zad; you had paid for the rahilah, for the ride. But now you are saying you need this money. So if you need this money and you need to dip into it, or need to take all of it — you cannot pay your rent, or you're having problems with your bills or whatnot — definitely there is no haraj whatsoever, there's no sin whatsoever, that you take from this money. And if by next year you are not able to save up enough to go for Hajj, the Hajj has been forgiven for you until you are able to save up, and there is no blame on you whatsoever.

> لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها

The Shari'ah is not something that is so difficult. So dear sister, do not feel any sense of blame, or any sense of haraj, as it is called in Arabic. Do not feel any sense of issue. There's no sin on you to take advantage of your own money for circumstances that have now occurred beyond your control. And if you're able to save up, alhamdulillah; if not, then whenever you can save up, then Hajj will become obligatory upon you. May Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala make it easy for all of us to perform the Hajj, insha'Allah, soon.
